title: ArcCivs warehouse capacity and bounded carpentry stock buffer
assumptions: Low/base/high sensitivity: 1/5/10 owners, one supplied carpenter, 0.25/1/4 active hours per day; not measured sessions.
Existing 60000 ms interval and native recipes remain unchanged: at most60 batches per carpenter-hour; hunger, route, stock capacity and ingredient availability reduce this.

Without outstanding demand baseline idle production is0. The buffer after change may use15/60/240 paid batches per operator-day only while a threshold is missing. Native planks4 per consumed log are the output envelope, not a mix of every recipe at once.

At most one warehouse per city holds a style-specific target:32planks,16sticks,12ladders,12slabs,8stairs,6fences,2gates,3doors,2trapdoors; level2 adds2chests+2barrels.97items total across11kinds; no lifetime grant or free material.

Stock on hand, in carpenter inventories, existing outputs and durable cargo is counted once. Ordinary/construction requests take priority. Missing source ingredients or destination capacity prevent buffer production.
Warehouse rack replacement increases physical slot capacity but does not create stocked items. A one-time bounded authored-rack migration must preserve nonempty/custom blocks.
Current SELL remains active; intended SELL-to-contract is a separate unchanged future scenario. No item-to-currency exchange or price change is inferred.

Verified warehouse added physical slots (levels1/2/3): Nordic486/1512/3078, Medievaloak324/378/486, Caledonia351/405/405; existing27-slot control barrel unchanged.339 authored rack cells become275 empty chests and64 air; no non-rack changes. MedievaloakL1:27→351 slots,0 stocked items issued.
